paragraphs.text: US market entry in 2027: whether and by which route
Discussion document for the CEO and board, March 2027 board meeting
Onsoo Botanicals
CEO Park Ji-won and the board
Built only from the briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, the only route within the board's limits; payback by 2030 needs ad cost held at the pilot's 28%
The US is worth entering: K-beauty is growing fast on Amazon, and Onsoo's pilot found demand
–	K-beauty sales reached $3.6B in 2025, 1.9 times 2021
–	Pilot units grew from 7,400 to 14,000 a month in six months
A national retail launch would break the cash cap, payback rule and margin floor
–	Retail-led cash crosses the $18M cap in 2029; group margin falls to 4.5% in 2027
Amazon-led fits all three limits and builds nearly four times the revenue of a Japan scale-up
–	At the pilot's ad cost, Amazon-led needs at most $2.4M and keeps margin above 8%
–	Japan adds $7M of revenue in 2030; the US route adds $26.4M
Its payback hinges on ad cost, and it reaches two-thirds of the $40M ambition by 2030
–	Payback needs ad cost below 28.6%; the agency median is 32%
–	Repeat purchase is 29%, against 48% in Korea
Approve the Amazon-led launch in March 2027, gating ad cost now and retail on awareness
–	Keep the CEO's plan, but move the retail trigger from 15% to 20% awareness

slides.title: BACKUP: Two figures circulated to the board should not drive the decision

paragraphs.text: 1 Opportunity    2 Retail-led    3 Amazon-led    4 Risks    5 Launch plan
BACKUP: Two figures circulated to the board should not drive the decision
The $5.2B market figure counts makeup and hair care
A 0.71 correlation does not show that doors drive Amazon sales
▪	A 2026 trade-press article puts the US K-beauty market at $5.2B in 2025
▪	That figure covers skincare, makeup and hair care sold by Korean brands
▪	Onsoo competes in facial skincare, where K-beauty brands sold $3.6B in 2025
▪	This deck sizes the market with the $3.6B facial skincare figure
▪	Across 30 K-beauty brands, more doors go with more Amazon sales
▪	Bigger, better-known brands win both doors and Amazon sales, so size can drive both
▪	Cause can run the other way: Saebom added 300 doors only after building about $30M of US revenue Amazon-first
▪	Option B's 1.3 times halo is therefore an assumption; without it, B loses even more cash
1  Briefing pack, section 12 and Table 9
